Performance evaluations are carried out by examining how different RIS element configurations affect SNR, eigenvalue distribution, and channel hardening. The results indicate that this approach significantly improves system performance by enhancing signal reliability and mitigating channel fading effects, positioning it as a strong solution for future RIS-based wireless networks.

articleTitle: A Music Recommender System to Identify the Emotional State of a Person Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: In today's digital world, customized recommendation algorithms can improve user experiences in many different areas. Within the sphere of intelligent human-technology interaction, this paper specifically examines a music recommender system driven by machine learning algorithms. It figures out what mood users are in and can provide an appropriate response in real time. The system being propounded in this essay uses advanced technology in facial expression recognition. With the help of a webcam, it aims to accurately detect user emotions, including joy, sadness, and anger. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) have been employed to effectively classify people's mood and recommend an appropriate song. Our extensive tests and examinations show that CNN, RNN, and SVM models are all very good at guessing users' moods--with high precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy percentages. Furthermore, in-depth analyses like confusion matrixes illuminate how well each model serves as an emotion recognizer. This study's findings are representative of future prospects in affective computing around the globe with major implications for intelligent recommendation systems to which it's important that the models are sensitive. In conclusion, the suggested Music Recommender System is something new for taking a more personal view: We can be as deeply entertained as the web allows us to be--make tailored entertainment paths in the digital era.

articleTitle: Real-Time Gesture Analysis for Evaluating Student Performance and Engagement
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: This paper is an extension of the practical application of computer vision and machine learning in monitoring student performance with the help of nonverbal communication, body language, and facial expressions analysis. The real-time visual input is processed within the system which identifies various postures and gestures by integrating Python packages such as OpenCV, MediaPipe, NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn. MediaPipe's holistic framework detects 3D landmarks that dynamically capture the body and facial expressions of students. These are then paired with machine learning models to predict behavior in terms of student engagement, attention levels, and participation. The traditional methods of classroom observation rely more on subjective interpretations, which have led to many inconsistencies. The project eliminates the limitations by automatically analyzing nonverbal cues, thus allowing educators to make objective observations about students' behavior. The data gathered is systematically classified into predefined categories by using the Ridge Classifier algorithm for high accuracy and interpretability. The study provides the possibility that such a system can help teachers trace learning issues and improve teaching techniques. It, however, displays possible applications besides education, which include criminal investigation, cooperative assessment of tasks, and remote observation in virtual areas. This advancement in technology increases the interface between AI and education. It shows an ability to affect the traditional methodologies of assessment used in education.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Emotion Recognition Using Morlet Dual-Level Wavelet Contextual Neural Network with Snow Geese Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: EEG-based Emotion Recognition (ER) works by analyzing brainwave patterns from EEG signals to understand and identify a person's emotional state. The problem of emotion identification from EEG signals remains challenging because brain activity presents both non-linear dynamic properties and individual-specific EEG patterns along with biological noise. Traditional approaches to emotion detection become inefficient due to EEG signal complexity thereby complicating accuracy and reliability measures. To tackle the challenges in EEG-based emotion recognition, this study presents a new approach called the Morlet Dual-level Wavelet Contextual Neural Network with Snow Geese Algorithm (MorDWCNNet+SGA). The method uses the SEED dataset, starting with preprocessing through the Observability-Constrained Resampling-Free Cubature Kalman Filter (OCRCKF) to enhance important EEG patterns. For feature extraction, the Multi-Discrete Wavelet Transform (MDWT) is applied to capture key EEG characteristics. Emotion classification is then performed using the Morlet Dual-level Wavelet Contextual Neural Network (MorDWCNNet), which is further optimized by the Snow Geese Algorithm (SGA) to improve accuracy. Implemented in Python and tested on the SEED dataset, the MorDWCNNet+SGA framework achieves remarkable results, with 99.9% accuracy and 99.3% sensitivity, significantly outperforming existing methods. The outcomes of the proposed method achieved high accuracy in effectively distinguishing emotional states through brainwave patterns. This method demonstrates how advanced techniques can combine synergistically to enhance ER performance resulting in improved real-world application accuracy and speed.

Author Keywords: Morlet Dual-level Wavelet Contextual Neural Network

articleTitle: A Semantic Driven Framework for Energy Efficient Task Scheduling in Dynamic Cloud Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: The rapid expansion of cloud computing has led to increased energy consumption, raising concerns about its environmental impact. Despite advancements in scheduling algorithms, existing methods face critical challenges, including suboptimal energy efficiency, limited adaptability to dynamic cloud environments, and insufficient context-aware decision-making. Recent techniques, such as Meta Reinforcement Learning, Genetic Algorithms, and Energy-Aware Scheduling, show potential but often struggle with high computational complexity, static resource allocation, or scalability issues. These shortcomings result in inefficient resource utilization, elevated energy usage, and difficulties in meeting Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements. To address these challenges, this study introduces the Energy Efficient Semantic Scheduling Framework (ESSF), a novel approach combining semantic reasoning and energy profiling to optimize task scheduling in dynamic cloud environments. The framework integrates three key components: (1) Dynamic Energy Profiling (DEP) for real-time energy monitoring, (2) Semantic Resource Matching (SRM) utilizing knowledge graphs for context-aware allocation, and (3) Adaptive Workload Balancing (AWB) to dynamically redistribute tasks for improved resource utilization and energy efficiency. Experiments using the Google Cluster Trace Dataset demonstrate that ESSF reduces energy consumption by up to 25% compared to traditional methods while achieving 90% resource utilization and 97% SLA compliance. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework to overcome existing limitations, offering a scalable, adaptive, and environmentally sustainable solution for task scheduling in cloud computing.

articleTitle: Stacking Based Enhanced Sales Forecasting for E-commerce Using Ensemble Learning approaches with Multi-Scaling Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: E-commerce and demand forecasting for large retail chains have taken the center stage in many business spheres. Sales prediction is one of the most important tools in inventory management and optimization of operations in retailing. This paper rates the applicability of some of the machine learning algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Import Vector Machine (IVM), and Multi-Scaled Long Short-Term Memory (MLSTM) based on the ability to predict sales of big marts. Though the basic idea of LR was satisfactory, it was deficient in terms of non-linearity and categorical features, which resulted in suboptimal performance on the problem set with a high value of RMSE as 1142.004 and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value as very low at 0.567 on the test data. Traditional models like Linear Regression struggle with non-linear relationships in sales data, leading to suboptimal performance. The superior handling of complex relationships through SVM turned out to be better than others with RMSE at 1133.55 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.574. SVM is Effective for handling high-dimensional data but limited in capturing temporal dependencies. The MLSTM model designed to capture the temporal dependencies has had an improved accuracy with RMSE = 1086.291 and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.6. LSTM networks are good at capturing temporal patterns but may struggle with multi-scale time dependencies. An ensemble model of LR, SVM, and MLSTM using stacking was developed. In the proposed method, each base model has been orchestrated to exploit its strength, achieving better performance of RMSE = 1050.20, MAE = 720.35 and with the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of the test data as 0.65. The developed ensemble model that combines Linear Regression, SVM, and Multi-Scaled LSTM to overcome these challenges and improve sales forecasting accuracy. The scatter plot of the predicted values against the observed ones, for the ensemble model, closely followed the ideal line, therefore, showing strong predictability and stability. The method easily overcomes the weaknesses in standalone individual models and provides a more reliable and accurate tool for the forecasting of e-commerce sales and demand planning.

articleTitle: Enhancing Connectivity of AODV in Urban Scenarios for VANETs: A QoS-Aware Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: As cities expand, vehicles and congestion become more complex. Efficient vehicle-to-vehicle contact networks are needed for road safety and efficient traffic flow. Thus, Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks are needed to overcome all the issues. The Adhoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV) routing protocol is used in VANETs. However, this protocol has many challenges in urban settings due to high vehicle density, rapid topology changes, and non-line-of-sight conditions. This work improves AODV by integrating Quality of Service (QoS) metrics. The prioritizing factors such as overhead and end-to-end delay are used to create a more efficient protocol for urban traffic. The SUMO simulator is used for realistic traffic patterns and NS-2 for network analysis. An evaluation of the protocol against the classical AODV is done and important metrics for real-time communication are focused. The enhanced AODV showed marked improvements. It achieved lower overhead in route finding, an increase in the number of packets sent, and lower end-to-end delay.

articleTitle: Dual-Stage Interleaved On-board Charger for Electric Vehicle using Snow Geese Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: The growing demand for electric vehicles (EVs) has highlighted the need for efficient and reliable on-board chargers (OBCs) to reduce charging time and enhance battery life. Nevertheless, there are some issues in classic OBC designs: harmonic distortion may become too large, electromagnetic interference increases, and thermal management is not proper; all of which directly affects other elements of the system. As an optimization approach to enhance the performance of the dual-stage interleaved on-board charger (OBC) for electric vehicles (EVs), this work introduces the Snow Geese Algorithm (SGA). The objective of the proposed method is to enhance charging efficiency and minimize cost. The proposed SGA is used to optimize the dual-stage interleaved converter, focusing on reliable performance and effective operation within EV charging systems. The suggested approach is then put into practice on the MATLAB platform and contrasted with a number of current techniques, including Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), Simulated Annealing (SA), Multi-objective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The proposed SGO method for dual-stage interleaved EV chargers achieves a cost of $1,050.80 and an efficiency of 97.2 %, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing expenses while maximizing optimization performance in charging systems.

articleTitle: Reliable Roadside Assistance and Fast Solutions for Emergency Breakdown States by EF-YOLOv8m
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: In the technological development era and fast-paced world, Artificial Intelligence techniques and Computer Vision algorithms are transfiguring the automotive industrial services, especially in reliable roadside assistance and emergency services for vehicle breakdowns. Significant AI-oriented algorithms including predictive maintenance, route optimization, resource allocation, and reinforcement learning techniques are used to address crucial problems like optimized resource distribution, rapid response, and proactive fault detection. This article incorporates AI-oriented algorithms for enhancing the accuracy, responsiveness, and efficiency of reliable roadside assistance and fast solutions for emergency breakdown states using the EF-YOLOv8m (Efficient - You Only Look Once version 8) algorithm. This proposed algorithm facilitates the visual prediction of breakdown situations and provides a fast solution for real-time prediction, analysis, and response in emergencies. The deployment of the EF - YOLOv8m algorithm leads to accurate prediction of vehicle breakdown situations, estimates road conditions, and detects critical faults to ensure the optimization of resource allocation and fast decision-making. Using its greater speed, accuracy, and lightweight model architecture, EE-YOLOv8 may process real-time image/video inputs and sensor data from vehicle-attached cameras, IoT devices, and surveillance drones in real time. Based on performance metrics such as confidence scores, detection accuracy, and frames per second (FPS), this model is used to analyse the reliability of EF-YOLOv8m in dynamic roadside environments. Additionally, the incorporation of AI -oriented and predictive maintenance algorithms improves the effectiveness of dispatch functions, reducing delay and guaranteeing timely assistance. Experimental results show the potential of YOLOv8m to transfigure the services of roadside assistance and provide an ascendable, high-performance solution that can address the difficulties of emergency breakdown situations with reliability and precision.

articleTitle: Enhancing Pneumonia Treatment in Children by Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Pneumonia is a health challenge that affects many people more so the children, thus leading to high death rates across the world. There is a persuading evidential proof which shows that the techniques in the application of the Machine Learning (ML) have helped in improving the diagnosis and treatment of pneumonia. This paper discusses a number of ML techniques such as CNNs, SVMs and Random Forest that can be used to enhance the reliability and effectiveness of detecting pneumonia from enhanced chest x-ray images. The classification shows how other methods like Min-Max normalization and a specific type of image pre-processing called Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) can make image quality even better as well as increase the accuracy of the model. Here, by using the sophisticated dalliance of ML models it is possible to dramatically minimize the incidence of diagnostic errors and enhance the results of pneumonia treatments thus witnessing an important evolutionary leap in the specialty.

articleTitle: A Review on the Role of Blockchain Technology for Decentralized Identity Management: A Future Without Passwords
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Advanced identity mechanisms are essential for secure client-identifiable proof in the unambiguously computerized world. Because the board frameworks rely on aggregated databases, fraud, data breaches, and unauthorized access are significant security risks. By providing a decentralized, immutable structure, blockchain technology advances security and protection. Through Self-Sovereign Identity, blockchain gives people authority over their own data. While also improving confirmation and check mechanisms. The potential of blockchain-based Identity, this article examines the board frameworks, focusing on five essential components: authentication, privacy, trust, integrity, and simplicity. It examines how interoperability, flexibility, and collaboration with outdated frameworks prevent decentralized IDMS being more widely used. The study also covers customer satisfaction, legal concerns, and potential future developments, such as Web 3.0, security enhancements, and integration with decentralized money. By addressing these problems and looking into new possibilities, blockchain-based IDMS may be able to reform advanced identity across the entire board.

articleTitle: Hands-Free Smart Glass for the Visually Impaired with Real-Time Obstacle Detection and Traffic Light Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: The Hands-Free Smart Glass for the Visually Impaired with Real-Time Obstacle Detection and Traffic Light Recognition is a lightweight, wearable device integrating ultrasonic sensors, ESP32-CAM modules for traffic light recognition, and a Text-to-Speech (TTS) system. The advanced real-time technologies used will address the problems of existing systems, such as limited detection of transparent or elevated obstacles and outdoor usability. Ultrasonic sensors can detect obstacles and determine the distances from them using the principle of Time of Flight, whereas the ESP32-CAM module classifies the traffic lights to improve navigation. The data is sent to the receiver in the form of clear audible instructions, like “Obstacle 1 meter ahead.” It eliminates the constraints associated with the use of white canes, as these are confined to obstacles within ground level only. Designed for extended periods of comfort and practicality, the system is user-friendly in both indoor and outdoor environments. Real-life testing showed obstacle detection accuracy to be 94% with nearly instant feedback. The solution, which addresses many key gaps between accessibility and safety, greatly increases mobility, independence, and users' confidence while navigating.

articleTitle: Generative Vision Hybrid Model Enhancing Realistic Synthetic Media Creation Through Advanced Image Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: In recent years, synthetic media generation has gained significant attention in areas such as entertainment, gaming, and visual content creation. The Generative Vision Hybrid Model leverages advanced generative architectures and image processing techniques to create highly realistic synthetic media. By integrating StyleGAN with a vision enhancement layer comprising Autoencoder-based Attention and Transformer modules, the model achieves exceptional quality in image synthesis. The dataset underwent robust preprocessing, including Wavelet Transform-based Noise Reduction and Adaptive Contrast Enhancement (ACE), ensuring clean and diverse inputs. The model achieved an Inception Score (IS) of 9.5, a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) of 15.8, and a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 0.94, outperforming existing benchmarks like StyleGAN2. Human evaluators rated the model's output with an average realism score of 4.7/5, highlighting its superior perceptual quality. Additionally, PSNR reached 32.6 dB, demonstrating high fidelity. The results validate the effectiveness of the hybrid model in producing photorealistic synthetic media with fine-grained detail and structural consistency. Future work can extend this approach to multi-modal media synthesis, real-time applications, and ethical watermarking systems to ensure responsible usage.

articleTitle: An Optimal Real-Time Routing and Clustering Protocol for UAV Networks Based on Security
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks play an important role in different application areas such as military surveillance, emergency services, and infrastructure. However, these networks face significant challenges such as data leakage, unauthorized access, limited processing capacity, and energy constraints. Available techniques such as Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), hash-based techniques, and dynamic clustering algorithms have been proposed to enhance security and operational performance; however, they often encounter challenges concerning scalability, adaptability to real-time changes within the network, and resource-related constraints. This research presents a streamlined authentication framework with the intent to facilitate secure and effective functionalities in turbulent and fluctuating settings. The proposed protocol uses Dijkstra's algorithm for optimal real-time routing, Adaptive Optimization Clustering (AOC) for dynamic resource distribution, and K-means clustering for noise classification. The proposed methodology achieves substantial improvements in power efficiency, latency, and Packet Delivery Rate (PDR) due to reduced computational overhead as well as risks such as data interception and replay attacks. Simulation results conclude that the system suggested here would be secure, scalable, and energy-efficient to be used for applications in demanding scenarios, such as mission-critical scenarios.

articleTitle: An AI-Based Intrusion Prevention System to Enhance Cloud Security
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Data breaches have become increasingly prevalent in cloud environments, demanding robust security measures. In an era where data breaches pose significant threats to organizational security and individual privacy, the protection of sensitive data has become paramount. A comprehensive strategy is proposed for analyzing sensitive data and preventing intrusions using a multi-modal framework. The methodology integrates AI techniques, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for classification of data as sensitive/non-sensitive and Parameter Efficent Fine-Tuning(PEFT) for categorization of sensitive data. Additionally, organization-specific regular expression (regex) pattern matching algorithms are utilized. Together, these components form an Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) capable of quickly identifying and alerting against unauthorized changes, with a focus on detecting sensitive data. The system also addresses pivot attacks, where attackers exploit vulnerabilities to access data across servers within the same network. By representing system components and their relationships as graphs, our approach enhances the detection and prevention of such attacks. This graphical representation facilitates a better understanding of component relationships and helps identify redundant storage elements, optimizing resource allocation. Our rigorous evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach in mitigating data breach risks and protecting sensitive information.

articleTitle: AI-Progressions in Automated Facial Paralysis Evaluation: A Comprehensive Survey of Traditional to Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Deep learning mechanisms allow computers to solve complex real-time problems with complex neural networks, it employs a vital role in health sector, for assisting the medical practitioners with quick and accurate decision making. Various studies on this research area proves that deep learning approaches are more effective in detecting facial paralysis, a common visible symptom of acute stroke. The sealing sign of stroke is facial weakness which destroys the newline muscle movements in the face on one or both sides of the nerves in the brain stream. Accurate and timely detection is most important and need of the golden hour, to patients effectively. Human assessment and traditional diagnostic methods have demonstrated poor inter rated reliability, demanding improved diagnostic tools. By analysing facial asymmetry and other relevant features like Face feature analysis, extracting characteristics such as eye shape, movement, and wrinkles from static images to detect facial weakness is done using various deep learning techniques. This work encompass the real-time challenges such as curating datasets, ethical concerns and data privacy of patients. The objective of this paper is to review the potentiality of various traditional to deep learning algorithms in automising the facial paralysis detection for accurate stroke diagnosis in patients. AI models can provide objective assessments that enhance the reliability of stroke detection.

articleTitle: Advanced Cyberbullying Detection: Integrating Pytesseract, Demoji, and BERT for Comprehensive Textual and Visual Content Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: In recent years, Cyberbullying on social media platforms leads to serious problems among children such as mental and health issues. To overcome these issues an advanced approach for cyberbullying detection and analysis method is needed. Traditional methods of cyberbullying detection focus mainly on text, often overlooking the significance of visual elements such as images and emojis. While recent techniques leveraging Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Computer Vision have shown promise, they face several challenges. Demoji is utilized to decode and normalize emojis, which are frequently used to convey harmful messages. Additionally, emoji decoding tools like Demoji provide textual representations of emojis but it lack in the ability to infer their contextual intent. These limitations are further compounded by challenges such as detecting sarcasm, handling cultural variations, and processing real-time data at scale. To enhance the cyberbullying detection, an effective method is used by integrating three powerful tools such as Pytesseract, Demoji, and BERT, applied to textual and visual content. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this integrated methodology, showing improved detection accuracy compared to traditional text-based approaches. This system offers a promising step toward more robust and multi-faceted cyberbullying prevention strategies.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Childhood Malnutrition Using Survey Data and Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Children's physical, mental and emotional development depends heavily on sleep, with age-specific sleep needs fluctuating. Malnutrition may result from eating too little, absorbing nutrients poorly, being unwell, living in poverty or not knowing enough about nutrition. Food allergies and iron insufficiency are two examples of illnesses whose onsets might differ depending on environmental exposures and genetics. By providing proper diet, getting medical attention when necessary and encouraging healthy behaviors, parents play a crucial role in supporting their children's health. For children to grow and develop properly, they need meals high in fruits, vegetables, milk, protein, calcium, iron and fiber. Key advantages of a balanced diet include aiding bone formation, improving heart health and encouraging regular bowel motions and digestion. In general, children's general health and wellness depend on caregivers being aware of their dietary requirements and giving them the proper attention. The findings of the research imply that machine learning algorithms may be useful in understanding and predicting the prevalence of malnutrition in children. Furthermore, these algorithms could provide perceptive data that might help politicians create effective policies. In this research, we make use of five different machine learning algorithms. With a decision tree, the accuracy is 0.92%, followed by svm which provides 0.91%, KNN, which provides 0.84%, GBM classifier, which provides 0.79% and random forest, which provides 0.65%.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection using Histopathological Images
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Breast cancer remains a major global health problem, and accurate and timely diagnosis of the disease is critical for improved survival rates. While traditional diagnosis methods like mammography and biopsy are well established, they are usually plagued by high false-positive rates and failure to discriminate between subtle histopathological patterns. Deep learning has made significant progress in medical image classification over the last few years, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) like ResNet and DenseNet have been demonstrating promising results. However, single models are not without their weaknesses, including vanishing gradients in deeper networks and poor feature propagation. To address these challenges, we introduce an ensemble model of DenseNet and ResNet architectures for breast cancer classification using histopathological images of the BreaKHis dataset. DenseNet offers improved feature propagation through densely connected layers, while ResNet solves the degradation issue via residual connections. Our ensemble model leverages the complementary strengths of the two architectures to offer improved feature extraction and classification accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed ensemble model achieved an accuracy of 97.5%, outperforming the performance of the single DenseNet model (96.3%) and the single ResNet model (86.1%). This study demonstrates the potential of deep learning ensembles in improving the accuracy of breast cancer diagnosis and reducing misclassification in histopathological examination.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Model to Predict Information Technology Students Learning Style in Adaptive Learning Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: The personalization of learning and the diversity of learning styles among students have required pedagogical innovations in educational institutions. The emergence of disruptive technologies in education has accelerated the potential for course delivery dynamics in both online learning and traditional classrooms. Students in the 21st century possess distinct strengths and limitations and favor instructional methods that will effectively improve their academic performance. In the previous study where supervised learning algorithms were implemented, we achieved a relatively low accuracy. In this study, we proposed a deep learning Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) algorithm to predict the learning style of students using thirty-seven training set features. We employed the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to augment the synthetic data for the minority class and achieve dataset balance when constructing the classifier. The hyperparameter of the MLP algorithm was optimized by multiple tests with varying training and testing split ratios to enhance the algorithm's predictive accuracy. The accuracy results show an improvement of the MLP deep learning classifier over the ensemble AdaBoost (RF) algorithm by 36.2%. The other performance indicators, such as the F-measure and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) for the MLP, outperform the ensemble classifier and supervised learning techniques.

articleTitle: Emerging Innovations in Deep Learning for Video DeepFake Detection: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: The fast growth of artificial intelligence technology allowed researchers to develop highly believable deepfake media that causes significant privacy breaches while being used for legitimate educational and entertainment purposes. Modern deep generative models are evolving at a fast pace so detecting manipulated media has emerged as an essential requirement. An analysis examines the latest advancements in deepfake detection through an assessment of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods particularly outlined by transfer learning and transformer-based systems. The evaluation analyzes modern approaches that detect artificial auditory and visual abnormalities which also solve problems with restricted datasets and the challenges of cross-manipulation and adversarial resistance. This study merges current scholarly research to show how modern detection systems perform yet stresses that more trustworthy detection solutions with enhanced efficiency need to develop. The rise of digital media in society demands sustained investment for research and technology development in video security protection. The progress of advanced deepfakes calls for organization-wide innovations in detection frameworks using AI-based solutions that must be developed to minimize their threats to digital content protection.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Networks for Physiological Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: A critically important application for physiological signal analysis lies in very early diagnosis and monitoring of potential medical conditions: among others, in cardiac dysfunction. This article describes a novel ECG Signal Classifier based on Multi-Modal Graph Neural Networks. We represented the ECG signal as time graphs, the time steps having nodes, so the sequential interrelations are their edges, able to represent both kinds of dependencies inside and among them in such a neural model. The MM-GNN utilizes graph convolutional layers to aggregate node-level features and pooling mechanisms to extract global characteristics. Tested on a standardized ECG dataset, the model achieves 86.10% accuracy, 85.40% precision, 92.20% recall, and an F1-score of 88.67%, showing balanced performance in classifying normal and abnormal signals. This framework opens up the possibility of graph-based deep learning in healthcare and is likely to pave the way for advanced diagnostic and real-time monitoring systems. Future work will be extended to other physiological signals and modalities for better diagnosis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Employee Skills Inventory and Attrition Prediction for Human Resource Management
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Products that are in various stages of being prepared for sale are referred to as inventory in accounting. This includes raw materials and both finished and unfinished goods. Employee behavior in a business is one component of inventory handling. Employees are therefore considered an inventory that helps an organization grow. Therefore, the company should reduce staff attrition if it wants to remain competitive in the market. Attrition may be a significant problem for organizations, particularly if important personnel, technical staff, and skilled personnel depart in search of better opportunities elsewhere. As a result, replacing a skilled worker costs money. This research thus proposes a new Multichannel Fuzzy Poplar Squeeze Excitation Network for employee attrition behavior prediction that can help with decision-making in the Employee Skills Inventory for Human Resource Management. A multichannel squeeze-excitation network is optimized by the Poplar Optimization Algorithm and combined with fuzzy rule-based decision-making to provide actionable insights into organizational growth. Employee data is pre-processed using Min-Max Scalar Normalization, and relevant features are chosen through the Binary Light Spectrum Optimizer (BLSO). The optimized network predicts the attrition behaviors, with fuzzy rules giving interpretable decisions. The model obtained accuracy of 98.5%, precision 99%, recall 98.5%, specificity 98.5%, f1-score 98.5%, MSE 0.15, MAPE 0.1, and R2 0.60 for attrition prediction. The proposed system allows HR managers to predict potential attrition risks; improve employee retention, and direct workforce management strategies towards organizational objectives.

articleTitle: Real-Time Indoor Target Tracking Using IoT and Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Indoor target tracking presents significant challenges across various fields such as security surveillance, industrial automation, and healthcare. This research paper outlines the design and implementation of a reliable direction monitoring system aimed at achieving accurate indoor target tracking using IoT and wireless sensor networks. By utilizing advanced sensor technologies and sophisticated data processing algorithms, the proposed system enables real-time monitoring and precise localization of targets within indoor spaces. The combination of IoT devices and wireless sensor networks facilitates effective data collection, analysis, and visualization, thereby improving the overall performance of the monitoring system. The results indicate that the developed system is effective in accurately tracking and localizing targets, fulfilling the essential requirement for efficient indoor direction monitoring solutions. The paper concludes with a discussion on the practical implications and potential applications of this system, emphasizing its importance in enhancing indoor target localization across diverse sectors.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Enhanced Intrusion Detection for Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Modern cyber security relies heavily on intrusion detection systems or IDS. However there are a number of issues with traditional IDS techniques such as high false positive rates, issues with scalability and trouble identifying zero-day attacks. IDS performance has increased due to recent developments in machine learning (ML); however problems like imbalanced datasets and processing overhead still exist. This article proposes an ML-based intrusion detection system (IDS) that makes use of Extra Trees Classifier (ETC), Gaussian Naive Bayes, and AdaBoost to improve detection accuracy. The usefulness of the suggested model is demonstrated by comparison with current techniques which emphasize its better classification performance resilience in real-time intrusion detection scenarios and versatility in managing a variety cyberthreats.

articleTitle: Dual-Channel Convolutional Neural Network with Attention Pooling and Sand Cat Swarm Optimization for Incremental Land-Cover Classification in Satellite Image Patches
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Incremental Land-Cover Classification in satellite image patches concerns the categorization of different types of land cover in satellite images. Land cover mapping from satellite imagery has applications in environmental observation, planning and resource management, and disaster response. Current land cover change classification paradigms involve heavily sampled and trained state vector data models, which do not have provisions for dynamic updates consequent upon variation in the cover density sizes, seasonal changes, incremental growth of urban sprawl, deforestation, and other natural calamities. Since new satellite images become available often, retraining your models from the very beginning is both time-consuming and computationally expensive. To tackle these issues, we propose a Dual-Channel Convolutional Neural Network with Attention Pooling and Sand Cat Swarm Optimization (DualCCNNet-AP+SCSO) for incremental classification of land cover in satellite imagery patches. This methodology utilizes satellite image patches from the So2Sat image patch dataset, where images are initially preprocessed with Iterative Self-Guided Image Filtering (ISGIF). After preprocessing, the Spike-Driven Transformer (SDT) method extracts key features, which are then classified through the Dual-Channel Convolutional Neural Network with Attention Pooling (DualCCNNet-AP), fine-tuned by Sand Cat Swarm Optimization (SCSO) for accurate incremental land-cover classification. The DualCCNNet-AP+SCSO method is implemented in Python. The effectiveness of the proposed method was assessed on the So2Sat image patch dataset, where it achieved an impressive 99.9% accuracy and 99.5% recall, outperforming current techniques. Based on these conclusions about classification accuracy, it demonstrated that the proposed approach enables the effective classification of the change, especially in the smallest class of the land cover in the satellite image patches. The results of the proposed method were better, in terms of performance, incrementally increasing the classification of land-cover from satellite image patches. The outcomes are higher accuracy, fewer iterations to converge with the result, and better feature extraction in the presence of noise than classical methods of the classification tasks relating to land-cover mapping.

Author Keywords: Dual-Channel Convolutional Neural Network with Attention Pooling

articleTitle: Monocular Depth Estimation for UAV Navigation Using Segmental Fully Convolutional Prairie Dog Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) play an important role in very precise navigation for its usage in applications like disaster management, agricultural surveillance, and as delivery drones. Precise depth estimation is crucial for UAV to safely avoid obstacles and thus obtain proper paths for flying. Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE), is another method which is becoming popular due to its easy implementation as compared to stereo vision and LiDAR systems in which single camera depth information is inferred. However, found that there are still some problems in the current a few deep learning methods of MDE, including high computational cost, low prediction accuracy in dynamic conditions, and unsuitability for real-time or online applications. In order to solve these problems, the current research work introduces a Segmental Fully Convolutional Neural Network (SFCNN) tended by the Prairie Dog Optimization (PDO) for UAV flight. The block structure improves adaptability as well as computational complexity; PDO seeks to minimize network's parameters to increase the result precision of the depth forecast and lessen the computation time. tarting from this background, the proposed approach is intended to support lightweight real-time and reliable means for MDE to enhance UAV navigation in complex environments.

articleTitle: Unraveling Pulmonary Fibrosis Deep Learning Transfer Learning for Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Pulmonary Fibrosis is a chronic lung disease demands prompt diagnosis for effective management. The proposed model develops an automated system using deep learning for feature extraction and machine learning for classification, reducing reliance on manual assessments. In the context, we use InceptionV3, VGG16, and MobileNetV2 for feature extraction as they are constantly successful and able to detect fine-grained patterns from medical images. The extracted features are further analyzed with popular machine learning techniques including but not limited to Random Forest and SVM. The proposed new hybrid model, leads to a faster diagnosis even if it is comparatively more accurate, than the previously used models. The system performance are evaluated using the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. These are integrated into the Flask-based web application and it enables quick and accurate Pulmonary Fibrosis diagnosis, aiding timely treatment and better patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Leveraging Big Data Analytics and Applied Mathematics for Predictive Maintenance in Industrial Automation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Predictive maintenance of industrial automation systems has attracted much interest recently, owing to the potential benefits of reducing downtime and improving production efficiency. However, existing solutions are affected by many different types of problems, such as managing heterogeneous and huge-scale data from dispersed industrial sensors, realising real-time analysis in high-speed data streams, and, at the same time, preserving interpretability while employing advanced techniques like deep learning and distributed machine learning. The recent approaches also use deep neural networks for fault detection and anomaly-based models for early warning signal identification with federated learning to ensure privacy-preserving data sharing. These have inherent complications such as a high rate of false positives and data imbalance handling difficulty; besides that, it is not flexible enough with the changing dynamics of the industrial processes. This paper addresses these limits by introducing an innovative architecture that merges big data analytics with applied mathematics to enhance predictive maintenance tasks effectively. To this end, one integrates machine-learning models with physics-based models across diverse datasets to enhance prediction accuracy while reducing false alarms and thus enabling proactive maintenance scheduling. In so doing, this approach will aim at shattering the present system's weaknesses by delivering robust anomaly detection along with decreased operational expenses in a scalable manner, thereby playing an important role towards further smarter, self-configurable manufacturing within the Industry 4.0 movement.

articleTitle: Brain Imaging and GRU-CNN Hybrid Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Progression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease detection and classification using deep learning techniques offer significant advancements in early diagnosis and progression analysis of this neurodegenerative disorder. This approach leverages various medical imaging modalities such as MRI, PET, CT, and fMRI, alongside clinical data like cognitive test results and biomarkers, to assess brain changes associated with Alzheimer's. The focus is on classifying the disease into three stages: Mild, Moderate, and Severe, using advanced machine learning models. Deep learning techniques, such as EfficientNet B7 for 2D imaging and 3D CNNs for volumetric data, enable efficient feature extraction from medical scans. Additionally, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) with GRU layers are used to capture temporal patterns from longitudinal data, improving predictive accuracy. Hybrid models, combining CNNs with attention mechanisms, further enhance classification. The model uses a multi-class classification approach with Softmax activation to predict the likelihood of each stage of Alzheimer's disease. Performance evaluation includes key metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and AUC (Area Under the Curve). AUC can be calculated in two ways: individual AUC scores for each disease stage or a combined AUC for overall classification. This analysis provides a comprehensive understanding of the model's effectiveness in distinguishing between different stages of Alzheimer's. The results can be integrated into clinical workflows to assist healthcare professionals in diagnosing and monitoring Alzheimer's disease progression, offering a potential path toward more efficient and early intervention strategies.

articleTitle: Sustainable Crop Yield Forecasting with the Dual-Branch Geometric Progressive Feedback Cosine Convolutional Network Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Using deep learning algorithms to extract important agricultural traits has made crop production prediction based on environmental, soil, water, and crop parameters an important area of research. But conventional approaches have trouble creating a straight linear or non-linear mapping between yield values and raw data, and the quality of the characteristics that are extracted has a significant impact on how well they work. Deep reinforcement learning builds a strong prediction framework by combining the intelligence of deep learning with reinforcement learning to get beyond these drawbacks. In order to anticipate agricultural yields accurately and sustainably, this work aims to create a Dual-Branch Geometric Progressive Feedback Cosine Convolutional Network with Skill Optimization Algorithm (DB-GPFCNet-SOA). Robust Double-Weighted Guided Filtering (RDWGF) is used for data preprocessing in order to minimize noise and improve important components. To ensure a complete prediction model, the N-Branch retrieves local neighbor-based information while the C-Branch records global geometric properties. Moreover, the accuracy is enhanced by the SOA, which enhances loss parameters. The suggested model has RMSE of 0.25 and MAE of 0.15 with exceptional accuracy of 99.2%, precision of 99.1%, recall of 99%, and F1-score of 99%. These results validate the performance of the model, which renders it a suitable approach for real-time agricultural applications.

Author Keywords: Geometric Progressive Feedback Cosine Convolutional Network

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Supervised Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms for Diabetic Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Lack of insulin production and utilization can lead to diabetes, which is a major health issue. Currently, diagnostic procedures are typically invasive and have various disadvantages, such as cost. Although various machine learning models can perform well in the field, they tend to perform poorly when under-performing on the data. Currently, most diabetes-related procedures depend on blood glucose levels. These include laboratory tests and glucose meters, commonly used at home and in hospitals. Although these methods are relatively accurate, they have various disadvantages. Some of these include the time and expense involved in performing the procedure, the lack of skilled technicians, and the pain that comes with testing. By utilizing the latest advancements in machine learning, deep learning, and sensor technology, the present research proposed to develop a novel method for non-invasive diabetes detection. The method addresses some of the challenges faced by traditional machine learning techniques, such as its limited sensitivity and accuracy. Finally, the future directions are highlighted to improve the reliability of the detection process.

articleTitle: Person Re-Identification Using Siamese Triplet Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Due to the increasing demand for public safety and the rapid development of intelligent surveillance networks, the re-identification of individuals (Re-ID) has become one of the most important research topics in computer vision. Person re-identification (Re-ID) has a wide range of applications, which increases its popularity in recent studies. The main goal of person re-identification (Re-ID) is to retrieve people with the same identity from different cameras. In the open world, there are still some challenges. First, existing re-ID research usually assumes that only one-factor variable (view, clothing, pedestrian pose, pedestrian occlusion, image resolution, RGB/IR modality) changes, and ignores the complexity of multi-factor variables in the open world. Second, existing ID methods are overly dependent on clothing color and other obvious pedestrian features that can be easily obscured or changed. In addition, the lack of benchmark datasets that include multifactor variables hinders the practical application of ID in the open world. The proposed model uses a Deep learning model -Siamese triplet network to extract the features, and a similarity measure to re-identify the individual. The evaluation metrics used are cumulative matching features (CMC) and mean average precision (mAP). Preliminary results show that the model performs well in comparison to existing methods, and future work will focus on improving robustness under varying environmental conditions.

articleTitle: ParaMedNetX: A Deep Learning Framework for Pneumonia Classification Using Chest X-Rays
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Pneumonia impacts a large proportion of individuals, especially in developing countries and in areas with less health care infrastructure, contaminated land and unhealthy living conditions. It is diagnosed as an inflammation of lung's air sacs marking as a dangerous respiratory illness. Its detection can be unpredictable due to the chance of an unclear appearance of the disease in X-rays and hence can be misdiagnosed. Deep learning models are widely used for assisting in medical image analysis and have improved the accuracy and efficiency of pneumonia diagnosis, but often struggle with insufficient feature extraction, class imbalance, and the need for large, annotated datasets. To address these challenges, this work proposes a novel advanced deep convolutional neural network-ParaMedNetX developed to classify pneumonia from chest X-ray. ParaMedNetX combines traditional convolutional layers in parallel shape as well as deep and residual connections which help in feature representation and accuracy. The model score was compared to the existing convolutional neural network models and the results outperformed with 89% accuracy, average precision score of 88% and area under the curve value as 95.4%.

articleTitle: Cataract Detection and Classification Using YOLOv9 and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Cataracts, a common age-related eye condition characterized by the clouding of the eye's natural lens, can impair vision if left untreated. Advances in cataract surgery have significantly improved treatment outcomes, but complications like posterior capsule rupture (PCR) still pose risks. Early detection is crucial, and recent developments in machine learning, particularly the YOLOv9 deep learning model, have shown promise in automating cataract detection using medical images such as eye scans. YOLOv9 can be trained to identify cataracts by recognizing distinct features like lens cloudiness and opacities. By leveraging image classification techniques and data augmentation, YOLOv9 achieves high accuracy in real-time cataract detection, assisting healthcare professionals in timely diagnoses and improving clinical workflows. Additionally, this model supports telemedicine applications by enabling remote analysis, expanding access to ophthalmic care. This paper highlights the significance of automated cataract detection using YOLOv9, its impact on early diagnosis, and its potential to enhance patient outcomes in ophthalmology through efficient image classification systems.

articleTitle: Developing a Robust Intrusion Detection System Using SMOTE and Hybrid SVNN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated approach to build up IDS with proper effectiveness toward the rising need for strong network security. Network traffic anomaly detection and classification are one of the major aims and enhance the security layer against various types of cyber threats. This study is a methodical approach in which a diverse set of data is first extracted from Kaggle. The collected dataset is a comprehensive one that includes various kinds of network traffic data. The first step includes preprocessing the data, i.e., handling missing values, removing erroneous entries, and dealing with outliers using the Interquartile Range (IQR) method. To counter class imbalance, Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is utilized in generating synthetic samples in underrepresented classes for generalization of models. The feature selection algorithm relies on the Chi-Square Lasso Feature Selection method. This method unites Chi-Square tests to select statistically significant features with Lasso regularization for feature dimension reduction with the goal of overfitting minimization. For building models, a hybrid of Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbors, which is termed as SVNN, is used. By using soft voting to aggregate the outputs of SVM and KNN, the proposed SVNN model improves the prediction accuracy, the degree of robustness, and adaptability. The presented methodology has achieved high classification accuracy 93.28%, precision 93.49%, recall 93.28%, F1 score 93.23%, and low RMSE of 0.2592. These metrics demonstrate that the model is reliable and of practical use for intrusion detection in dynamic, high-dimensional environments of networks, providing a proper solution to modern security network challenges.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model for Enhanced Weather Forecasting: Leveraging Spatial and Temporal Dependencies
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Accurate weather forecasting is critical for decision-making in agriculture, disaster management, urban planning, and numerous other domains. Traditional forecasting methods often struggle to capture the intricate spatial and temporal dependencies in weather data. This work proposes a hybrid deep learning model that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to address these challenges. The CNN component efficiently extracts spatial features from satellite images, such as cloud formations and precipitation zones, while the LSTM network models the temporal dependencies inherent in meteorological data, such as temperature, humidity, and wind speed. The model is trained on a dataset comprising historical weather records and satellite imagery, spanning several years. PyTorch, a dynamic deep learning framework, is used to implement and train the hybrid architecture. Data preprocessing involves normalization, image augmentation, and sequence structuring to prepare inputs for the model. The CNN layers, built with convolutional and pooling operations, extract spatial features, which are combined with temporal weather data and passed to the LSTM network. The LSTM layers capture long-term dependencies and trends in weather patterns. Fully connected layers map the learned features to final predictions, including temperature, rainfall, and other key weather parameters. The hybrid model is evaluated using metrics such as Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) for numerical predictions and accuracy for classification tasks. Results indicate that the proposed hybrid CNN-LSTM model outperforms standalone models and traditional statistical approaches, demonstrating its ability to leverage spatial and temporal dependencies for accurate weather forecasting. This work highlights the potential of hybrid deep learning models in advancing weather forecasting capabilities, offering a scalable and reliable solution for real-world applications such as extreme weather event prediction and agricultural planning.

articleTitle: Optimized Stacked Sparse Autoencoder for IoT-Cloud Smart Healthcare Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: IoT technology growth in healthcare has been a revolution, and that is exciting, with the monitoring of real-time critical physiological and clinical parameters from real-time data: data-driven, personalized healthcare solutions. Even with such potential, health IoT faces challenges such as heterogeneity in data, noise, and inconsistent feature extraction that leads to suboptimal decision-making. Methods have to be developed efficiently for preprocessing and feature extraction to analyze data so that this disease can be predicted or monitored correctly. The motivation is to design a solid framework that bridges such gaps by making sure reliable, accurate predictions fit the smart healthcare application. Testing the proposed system with IoT-enabled wearable devices and clinical electronic health records (EHR), physiological metrics were collected from IoT sensors, supplemented by medical history and diagnostic data retrieved from cloud databases for blood pressure, heart rate, glucose levels, and oxygen saturation. The pre-processing step utilized Global-Local Depth Normalization (GLDN), which normalizes global structures and local variances to remove noise and scale variations. These features were analyzed using a Stacked Sparse Autoencoder (SSAE), optimized by Cat Hunting Optimization (CHO) to enhance prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Experimental results validate the system with a remarkable 99.7% accuracy, 98.1% precision, and 97.5% recall and reduces computation time by 22% compared to the existing techniques. This shows the robustness and feasibility of the proposed approach in applications of smart healthcare. In conclusion, this framework represents an effective solution for smart healthcare systems that deals with data heterogeneity and the challenge of feature optimization for better patient care and resource management in IoT-driven environments.

Author Keywords: Global-Local Depth Normalization Stacked Sparse Autoencoder

articleTitle: Innovative Object Detection with YOLOv4 and Adaptive Bounding Boxes
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: This research work proposes a computer vision-based object detection system. It can recognize each and every object visible in the picture. Horizontal boundary boxes were used to detect different objects available in the detectors. However, buildings and cars in the aerial imagery are occasionally very close to form continuous objects that may suggest a direction. Therefore, some approaches such as extending the horizontal bounding box to oriented box are proposed for a better object extraction; usually via directly regressing the angle or corners. Here we propose an orientation object detector which is simple but more accurate, and it is based on YOLOv4. Here yolov4 is used to detect objects yolo can able to find more than one object in a single image. The paper will contain specific implementation methodology for yolov4 with OpenCV, which includes model configuration settings, preprocessing steps and evaluation matrices such as mean average precision (map), recall and the precision. The object detection problem has transformed into a key problem in computer vision and has enabled improvements in areas including self-driving cars, medical systems, and even surveillance systems. In this paper, we present a new object detection system based on YOLOv4 which stands for ‘You Only Look Once’ version four and uses adaptive bounding boxes. The CSPDarknet-53 and spatial pyramid pooling (SPP) are the main reasons for YOLOv4's immense popularity, as is discussed in the literature. But with the constant changes of the bounding boxes, performance accuracy suffers greatly as they have a difficult time identifying the objects bounding boxes are placed within. To counter this problem, we present an explainable adaptive bounding box technique which relies heavily on the size shape and features of the context of the object being captured. The learnable bounding box adjustment layer which serves to refine the localized bounding boxes is integrated into the head of YOLOv4, where putting the primitive guesses goes through our specialized deep neural network so filters are set and only the most accurate localization guesses are retained. This method proves useful in more complicated scenarios with the presence of occlusions, multiple objects and changes in scale.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Feature Selection Model for Early Prediction of Metabolic Syndrome
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Metabolic Syndrome (MetS) is a medical condition that increases the risk of cardiovascular diseases, stroke, and type 2 diseases. Some of the symptoms of MetS are high blood pressure, elevated blood sugar, excess body fat, and abnormal cholesterol levels. All these symptoms are interconnected, which has made early diagnosis of MetS critical. In current medical strategies, there is no personalized medication which leads to unfavorable health outcomes and further increased risks. This paper aims to address these challenges by identifying optimal feature subsets required for the early prediction of MetS. To get the optimal features a hybrid model is proposed in this paper. The proposed model utilizes both the filter method and the wrapper method. Firstly, features are selected using the correlation coefficient (CC) method which is a filter method, and then the selected features are further refined using genetic algorithm (GA) which is a wrapper method. This hybrid model increases the prediction accuracy and reduces computational cost. The methodology of the proposed model, its experimental setup, the results obtained, and the inferences gained are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Detection of Emergency Vehicles in Traffic and Assign Traffic Free Path Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)

authors.preferredName: V T Ram Pavan Kumar M
P V V S D Nagendrudu

abstract: Too much of Traffic jams are in a highly populated country. Sometimes emergency vehicles such as fire-fighter and ambulance get stuck in traffic, putting lives at threat in many cases. Priority should be given to special vehicles and their way should be cleared. However, traffic police find it difficult or sometimes impossible to handle with it. Emergency vehicles have visual and audio warning devices help them to overtake traffic by demanding as little space as possible from other vehicles. Many death happen due to delay in doctors, ambulance and fire engine vehicles while reaching their destinations. The traditional systems didn't provide path free route accurately. Therefore, by using detection of emergency vehicles in traffic and assign traffic free path using deep learning system, emergency vehicles can get free path or fast route by observing the traffic cameras. So, those emergency vehicles can reach the location on time by using RNN system. Therefore, the main objective is to improve this system for better results interms of accuracy, detection rate and precision.

articleTitle: Enhancing Student Performance Prediction using E-Learning through Multimodal Data Integration and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Advanced machine learning techniques have shown significant promise in predicting student performance in E-Iearning systems, but challenges such as handling imbalanced datasets, integrating multimodal behavioral data, and managing the complexities of feature selection persist. Recent techniques, such as SMOTE for class balancing and BorutaNetCV for feature selection, have made strides in improving prediction accuracy; however, they often fail to address real-time cognitive state integration and the influence of diverse engagement patterns. To overcome these limitations, this study employs a comprehensive methodology that combines robust preprocessing methods, advanced feature selection, and ensemble machine learning models such as Random Forest, AdaBoost, and XGBoost. The findings demonstrate that predictive accuracy can be significantly enhanced through these techniques, and the proposed framework enables the development of personalized interventions that can foster improved student engagement and success in dynamic E-learning environments.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Road Safety: An Innovative Approach to Pothole Detection and Prevention Using XAI and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: This paper presents an automated pothole detection system using deep learning, and Explainable AI (XAI), which improves model transparency and decision-making. High-quality images and videos undergo image processing, including edge detection, feature extraction, and deep learning, enabling precise identification and classification of potholes, even in challenging environments. Evaluating potholes is crucial for road maintenance, safety, and reducing costs related to vehicle damage and road repairs. Traditional methods, such as manual inspections and sensors, are costly and time-consuming. The proposed real-time system can spot problem areas before they become severe potholes.

articleTitle: Framework for Drug User Analysis and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: This paper provides a framework for knowledge and action related to and about substance abuse, that integrates both capacity development and data-driven analysis for drug use analysis and modeling. In line with the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) the framework focuses on a multi-pronged strategy. It then gives examples of so-called capacity-building exercises, such as those carried out by Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham in Tamil Nadu in 2020. These programs targeted key stakeholders, including healthcare professionals, police personnel, teachers, and social workers, focusing on preventive education, medical management, psychosocial issues, and rehabilitation strategies related to substance abuse. Pre- and post-training evaluations showed a strong increase in participants knowledge and treatment skills for substance use disorders. Second, the paper presents a data-driven, quantitative analysis of drug use patterns and related factors. Using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm, the study utilizes a dataset of drug consumption patterns to determine the factors which are most important for drug consumption. Importantly, the framework also include Explainable AI (XAI) methods to increase the interpretability and tracibility of the machine learning model. XAI approaches are used to interpret the model's decision process and to identify the most important factors in predicting the use of drugs. Incorporating insights from the capacity-building program evaluation and from the XAI-aided machine learning analysis, this framework provides an integrated end-to-end framework for drug user analysis and the generation of actionable recommendations for the design of targeted interventions and prevention strategies.

articleTitle: Enhanced Ransomware Detection using a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Convolutional Neural Network with Boosted Sooty Tern Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: Ransomware attacks threaten organizations by encrypting files or locking systems and keeping them inaccessible unless a ransom is paid. Early detection of ransomware attacks helps organizations avoid financial losses, theft of data, and harm to their reputations. This early detection will also reduce the risks related to malicious activities. Detection by signature-based or heuristic approaches tends to be traditional and fails when evolvement in ransomware attacks is considered. Thus, a need for innovative techniques of deep learning and optimization algorithms can be observed. The method proposed in this study focuses on developing a novel multi-stage framework for detecting ransomware attacks. Firstly, correlation coefficient-based min-max normalization (CCMMN) for data preprocessing is used since it makes the data elements more uniform and makes the detection system more efficient. Feature selection is then carried out and optimized using the hybrid Osprey optimization algorithm with an enhancing sparrow search algorithm (OOA-ESSA) to arrive at the most relevant feature for classification. Last, this paper applies a hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural network with boosted sooty tern optimization (HQCCNN-BSTO) in ransomware detection. The classic model is replaced by a quantum and hybrid classical neural network that may be complemented by an optimization algorithm to increase the speed and efficiency of the detection. The method that has been proposed here offers a flexible and efficient approach to the problems associated with the detection of ransomware threats in the practical environment. Thus, high effectiveness is proved by the 99% accuracy rate of the suggested method. This exceptional outcome proves the robustness of the approach and its ability to adapt to various patterns of dependence and data changes.

articleTitle: IoT Based Monitoring System for Health During Menstruation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: The integration of IoT and ML brought forth new prospective solutions in menstrual health management, pertaining to continuous monitoring of physiological signals and personalization of insights for women. This article discusses the usage of IoT, smartphones, and cloud-based systems for tracking vital signs, temperature, pulse rate, and flow of menstruation that will enable pro-active management of the cycle. The use of ML algorithms, including supervised models-like Random Forest and Logistic Regression-and complex techniques like RNNs and LSTM networks-offers added advantages for predicting menstrual cycles and ovulation. These technologies offer personalized health recommendations, early diagnosis of menstrual disorders, and help in communicating with healthcare providers in a very short span of time. While offering huge potential to improve women's health, concerns around data privacy, ethical considerations, and equitable access to these digital health solutions are highlighted. The existing systems showed improvements yet they encountered problems because of insufficient data diversity and health system integration as well as insufficient personalization and imprecise cycle predictions. Data privacy issues and security threats that stem from ML models along with constant bias concerns prevent broad acceptance of ML systems in general use. This research study analyzes IoT and ML applications in menstrual health today and introduces their advantages as well as the barriers that require resolution before mass acceptance can occur. The proposal introduces an approach to create menstrual tracking software through a combination of rule-based systems with ML algorithms that generates precise forecasts alongside tailored information for women who have PCOS or PCOD.

articleTitle: The Role of AI and Machine Learning in Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
abstract: AI together with ML technology now provides detailed rapid medical data evaluation to enhance cancer diagnosis and treatment methods. Advanced algorithms installed in these technologies help medical staff identify cancer indicators which human experts commonly miss leading to better diagnostic accuracy. AI-powered Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) scan analysis allows doctors to perform quicker and more efficient medical diagnosis. The usage of ML models enables medical professionals to detect prognostic trace elements thus they can enhance treatment choices by analyzing tumor cell biological classification groups. AI actively participates in protein and gene targeting together with clinical trial planning to move personal cancer treatment forward. AI applications face multiple obstacles that stop their effective adoption in the field of oncology. The majority of present-day barriers to AI implementation in oncology stem from problems with data privacy together with algorithmic biases and model validation methods while the high complexity of systems and decreasing model interpretability specifically hinder usage. The success of AI models depends on extensive and diverse datasets although the actual availability of relevant data sets combined with standardization procedures continues to be difficult. Medical diagnostic applications where AI performs its decision-making work present important transparency issues that create doubts about its effectiveness. The analysis of data privacy through federated learning and XAI for interpretability and transfer learning for efficiency and deep learning for accuracy improvement are recent solutions being researched to resolve these problems. The primary aim of this research explores how AI and ML influence cancer diagnosis together with treatment methods while studying present challenges alongside suggested methods to boost their operational performance. The combination of better data governance together with ethical AI frameworks and model validation protocols makes way for AI and ML to remodel oncology practice with highly personalized efficient trustworthy cancer care solutions.

articleTitle: Extracting Crucial Information from Lengthy Transcripts Using Text Summarisation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Sentiment Analysis and Deep Learning (ICSADL)
